definitions.explanation: A bath for soaking and washing, or the act of taking a bath. In Japan, bathing typically involves washing the body outside the tub before soaking in hot water.

examples.japanese: お{風呂|ふろ}が{沸|わ}いたよ。
{仕事|しごと}の{後|あと}はゆっくりお{風呂|ふろ}に{浸|つ}かるのが{一番|いちばん}の{楽|たの}しみだ。
examples.english: Soaking in the bath after work is my greatest pleasure.

notes:
Usually preceded by the polite prefix お as お{風呂|ふろ}, even in casual speech.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- お{風呂|ふろ}に{入|はい}る (take a bath)
- お{風呂|ふろ}を{沸|わ}かす (draw/heat a bath)
- お{風呂|ふろ}が{沸|わ}く (the bath is ready)
- お{風呂|ふろ}に{浸|つ}かる (soak in the bath)
- お{風呂|ふろ}を{掃除|そうじ}する (clean the bathtub)

In Japanese homes, the bathwater is shared by the family, so people wash and rinse outside the tub before soaking. {銭湯|せんとう} (public bathhouse) and {温泉|おんせん} (hot spring) follow the same etiquette.
